scenarios.hypothesis: An active fire produces the frozen burning transition while the no-active-process control does not progress.
A recorded support loss makes the supported structure unstable with complete causal attribution.
One active spread process covers every frozen propagation target without adding another target.
A character and fall process claiming one posture in the same bucket remain contested and emit no world patch.
Swapping the character actor label leaves the world receipt and contested claims unchanged.
A character claim in a later turn does not suppress an earlier fall process.
Observed airflow may refine an unknown spread trigger once without rewriting a known state.
Inactive and untriggered processes terminate as rejected receipts without effects.
Missing rules, out-of-scope targets, and invalid concretization fail closed without environmental inventions.

decision.label: supported
reasons: Shadow cost and complexity ceilings passed.

limitations: The semantic judge is a proxy and cannot establish an objectively correct final battle result.
Rules, triggers, targets, character claims, and the one concretization are pre-authored fixtures.
Local latency excludes persistence, concurrency, provider, and production load.
No runtime, canonical commit, persistence, provider ordering, release, or deployment behavior is changed.
